label: TP
reason: Both alerts indicate real vulnerabilities. The XSS alert (java/xss) traces user input from getParameter -> map32515.put('keyB-32515', param) -> map32515.get('keyB-32515') -> bar -> sql -> response.getWriter().println(...+sql...). The resolved sink value includes raw user input directly in HTML output, bypassing the ESAPI encoder which is called only in the EmptyResultDataAccessException block. The SQL injection alert (java/sql-injection) traces user input from getParameter -> map32515.put('keyB-32515', param) -> map32515.get('keyB-32515') -> bar -> sql. The resolved sink value 'SELECT ... where USERNAME=\'foo\' and PASSWORD=\'' + bar + '\''' contains attacker-controlled data, enabling SQL injection.

evidence.note: User input flows through map32515.get('keyB-32515') to bar, then into unsanitized SQL query string printed to writer in normal execution path (line 77-79), confirming both XSS and SQLi risks.
XSS sink: response.getWriter().println concatenates raw bar (tainted) into HTML output. Encoder is only used in exception handler, leaving main path vulnerable.
